Chapter 10: Living Out Enough—Impacting Others and the World
When your confidence starts to grow, it doesn’t just stay tucked away inside. The freedom that comes from knowing you’re enough? It spills over into every part of your life—your relationships, your work, and even the world around you. People who truly understand their worth become these amazing sources of encouragement, compassion, and hope for everyone they meet.
Picture a teacher who once struggled with self-doubt. Now, she sees her students in a brand new light. She notices the quiet kids—the ones who might feel invisible—and goes out of her way to offer words of affirmation. Her own journey gives her the chance to give what she once needed most: a gentle reminder that every person matters.
Or imagine a business leader who’s let go of the constant need to prove herself. She builds a culture of grace in her workplace, where mistakes aren’t met with shame, but with understanding. Sure, success is celebrated, but not at the cost of kindness. And the ripple effect? It’s incredible. When people feel safe to be themselves, creativity and collaboration just take off.
Most of us don’t realize the true impact of living from a place of enough. It changes the way we parent, the way we love, and the way we serve others. It lets us show up fully—without fear, and without pretending. And honestly, the world is hungry for this kind of authenticity and hope. When you dare to believe that you’re enough, you can change lives.
Here’s something to remember—this isn’t about being perfect, or having all the answers. It’s about being present, willing to offer what you have, just as you are. Sure, the journey isn’t over; there will always be new challenges and fresh opportunities to practice living out enough. But your foundation is solid. Your worth isn’t up for debate. It’s given, unshakeable—and it’s meant to be shared.
